source: MAFF General Directorate of Agriculture, banana cultivation techniques manual, 2019, section V.1.3 (freckle / speckle disease)
text:
Freckle disease is caused by the fungus Guignardia musae. It produces distinctive clusters of small, dark, raised spots scattered across the leaf and fruit surface, often following the pattern of leaf veins, with affected areas sometimes showing a rust-brown or yellowish tinge, particularly near leaf tips as the infection develops. On fruit, the spotting is mainly cosmetic but can affect market appearance and, in the Cavendish-type varieties especially, is taken seriously by growers aiming for export-quality fruit.

Prevention and control: cut off and destroy infected leaves as soon as symptoms are seen, and apply the fungicide Maneb for farmers with access to agricultural chemicals, following label directions.
